result.rationale: The diff shows `const isTeamAdminOrOwner = (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...));` — the variable is named 'isTeamAdminOrOwner' but the `&&` requires the user to be BOTH an admin AND an owner, so a mere admin (or mere owner) would be denied. This contradicts the intended OR semantics, and given owners are typically also admins, effectively only owners pass — a real authorization-logic defect in the new addGuests handler.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be BOTH a team admin and a team owner. Given the variable name and the subsequent permission gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)`, this will incorrectly deny access to users who are only admins or only owners (a common role model). This is a concrete logic issue introduced in the new handler.
